reason: E2 shows Sc addition creates a two-phase bcc+hcp structure where superconductivity originates from the bcc phase with parameters identical to the parent alloy, directly contradicting the premise that the secondary phase degrades superconductivity. E1 only confirms a single-phase bcc HEA is superconducting, offering no support for the degradation mechanism.
premises: Superconductivity in bcc HEAs relies on a phonon-mediated pairing network provided by the bcc lattice.
A secondary hcp phase does not support superconductivity.
Introducing a secondary hcp phase disrupts the continuous electron–phonon coupling network.
Interfaces from the secondary phase scatter Cooper pairs, reducing Tc and Hc2.
Sc addition promotes hcp phase formation in Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr HEAs.
